rationale: The plan correctly identifies that a 1-vs-1 design supports no inference, explicitly forbids DESeq()/results()/lfcShrink/edgeR/limma, and delivers only size-factor-normalized counts and descriptive log2(treated/control) ratios with a stated pseudocount and expression floor, while naming >=3 biological replicates per condition as the design that would support testing. QC is adapted to the design (library sizes, detection, quantiles, top-gene share, blind VST correlation/distance, MA plot) with an explicit statement that PCA and within-group clustering are undefined at n=1 rather than silent omission; the >=10 counts in >=1 sample filter is minimal and justified by smallest group size, and normalization is median-of-ratios computed inside DESeq2 with no pre-scaling, plus an honest note on the missing tximport offsets. The reference level is set explicitly to control with the contrast direction written out, and the absence of p-values/FDR is stated as a consequence of the design rather than an oversight. The weak point is the enrichment step: although it is well-specified (full ranked list, tested-gene universe, 15-500 size window, named collections with versions, seed, unmapped share, no ORA), running fgsea on a descriptive 1-vs-1 ranking generates permutation p-values that the reference would not warrant here, and the 'descriptive ordering only' label mitigates but does not remove that risk.
